messages:
SRE-Oncall: :rotating_light: Paging — seeing sustained NCCL stalls + runaway KV cache growth starting ~00:12 UTC. p95 token latency jumped, some requests returning 503s. Suspect interaction between continuous-batching heuristic and TP KV-sharding (uneven partitioning).

incident-bot: Incident created (sev2) — KV-cache / TP-shard imbalance -> NCCL stalls. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-tp-nccl>.

SRE-Oncall: @Carla @Dave can you take primary/secondary? I'm on triage but need infra handoff for hotfix.

Carla: Taking primary. grabbing logs & flamegraphs now. I can also push a quick config rollback if needed.

Ben: Observed cache blowup on tp-group-3: gpu5 memory 98% while peers 30-50%. NCCL stall counters spiking on node-7.

Emma: Batch distribution looks skewed — continuous batching coalesced several long-context requests into the same batch, blowing KV footprint per shard.

Carla: Mitigation plan (short):
1) disable continuous batching globally
2) set KV_SHARD_STRATEGY=local (fallback to per-GPU local shards)
3) cap per-shard KV memory with env KV_MAX_BYTES=6GB
I'll roll env change to rt-infer deployment.

Dave: Need customer impact numbers before we push. which tenants saw 503s / errors?

SRE-Oncall: Preliminary: AcmeSearch and NovaHealth experienced 503s 00:15-00:22 UTC. ~0.8% of their requests, overall platform error rate +0.6%. Hosted free-tier latency increased.

Carla: Executing hotfix — command:```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/rt-infer CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false KV_SHARD_STRATEGY=local KV_MAX_BYTES=64424509440 --record
```
Rolling to us-west-2 first.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: rt-infer (us-west-2) — 1/12 -> 6/12 pods updated.

Ben: Metrics update: 60s after env flip, NCCL stall rate dropped to ~0, GPU mem across group normalized. Latency trending back to baseline.

Emma: Did a targeted canary re-enable of continuous batching on a single node with KV_SHARD_STRATEGY=round_robin — it reproduced the memory skew. Hypothesis holds: round_robin + long seqs -> uneven KV partitioning.

Carla: Temporary mitigation confirmed. Next steps: revert continuous batching global flag only after we have a shard-aware batching change. Opening a PR to compute shard keys by prefix-hash of sequence IDs rather than round-robin. PR: <https://redwood.internal/pull/infra/kv-shard-hash-pref>.

Dave: Oncall handoff to @Frank in 30m. Frank — keep autoscale paused for tp-group-3 and watch NCCL counters.

Frank: Acknowledged. Will monitor. I'll also add an alert that fires if shard memory variance > 30%.

SRE-Oncall: Customer comms: Ben, please coordinate with Support to notify AcmeSearch/NovaHealth with root-cause + mitigation summary.

Ben: Draft sent to Support. They confirm both customers saw <1% errors and accept incident comms.

Carla: Diagnostic checklist saved: heap dumps from affected GPU pods, NCCL traces, batch composition sampling, per-tenant KV usage. Also created reproducer job to simulate long-context batch coalescing.

Support: Acknowledged receipt of comms. Customers asked for ETA on permanent fix; we replied we'll follow up in postmortem next 72h.

Emma: Long term fixes to track:
- shard-aware batching (avoid grouping many long contexts into same shard)
- deterministic shard assignment using sequence-prefix hashing
- backpressure throttle for continuous-batching when per-shard memory > threshold
- add unit/regression tests for perf cliffs triggered by batching + sharding combos.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to "mitigated" at 00:40 UTC. Investigation active.

SRE-Oncall: Thanks team. Action items: Carla to merge hotfix PR and coordinate permanent change, Emma to own test harness and regressions, Ben to close loop on customer comms, Frank to adjust alerting. Follow-up postmortem draft due EOD.

Carla: Uploaded logs and NCCL traces to incident folder: /incidents/2370000000/artifacts. Added reproducer command:```bash
python infra/tools/kv_repro.py --tp-group tp-group-3 --seq-lens 1024,2048,8192 --continuous-batching 1 --clients 50
```

Ben: Closing notes: Hotfix prevented further customer impact. We should add a canary gate that prevents continuous-batching from rolling to clusters with >X% shard variance.

SRE-Oncall: Agreed. Closing the chat, will publish postmortem. Great coordination — :thumbsup:
